messages:
vivian: quick sync two date-selector patterns for the invoices panel: timeline slider vs calendar grid. prototyped both. slider is exploratory, calendar is exact. link: https://figma.com/file/slider-vs-calendar omar: slider is awesome for spotting spikes quickly, but accountants expect month boundaries for exports. can slider snap to months? felix: +1 for snap. also propose a month-chip fallback: when slider is near a month boundary show a chip: `Mar 2025` that you can click to snap. keeps both behaviors. tara: can we add a heatmap under the slider showing daily spend intensity? that makes spikes obvious and gives context without leaving panel. billing-bot: FYI: current export pipeline accepts arbitrary ISO ranges for CSV; invoice PDF export is month-bucketed. if UI sends non-month ranges we generate pro-rated PDFs (support asked for clarification). vivian: good to know. UX decision: slider should snap to month by default but allow fine-grain drag when users hold `Shift` (like precision-drag). show a tooltip "Hold Shift for day-level". omar: accessibility nit: slider must be keyboard-draggable and expose `aria-valuetext` with human date (e.g., "Start date: March 1, 2025"). heatmap cells should have `role=gridcell` + `aria-label` with date and $ amount. felix: code example for aria on slider we can reuse: ```
...
``` (we'll map to epoch or ISO depending on lib) tara: copy tweak: change CTA from `Export` to explicit options: `Download invoices (PDF)` and `Download ledger (CSV)`. add small helper: "PDFs are month-based; CSV is line-item ledger." this should reduce support confusion. billing-bot: Suggestion: if user requests >12 months, auto-queue and show "We'll email you when ready" instead of immediate download. large exports timeout. vivian: plan: implement slider with month-snap + Shift for day-precision, add heatmap under slider, keyboard and aria updates, explicit invoice CTAs, and queueing for big exports. i'll update figma and break into tickets. omar: sounds good, please add an a11y PR review step. felix: i'll draft the aria guidance and paste examples in the ticket. tara: i'll do a quick usability test with a couple finance users once dev preview is available. billing-bot: Prototype updated: https://figma.com/file/abcd-invoice-timeline (pinned by @vivian).
